method: A nonlinguistic typesetter samples tokens independently from the public practice-training paragraph vocabulary, weighted by occurrence. For each new line it chooses a random capacity of 35–55 transcription characters including spaces. It samples up to five candidate words for the remaining space, writes the first that fits, and ends the line if none fit. A candidate completing a four-word manuscript phrase is also rejected as required by the guard. Seed 23017, 2,600 generated lines. This is a capacity-and-retry model: it uses no word-length threshold and no rule that places a short word last, but it is an exploratory model chosen to test the positional fact; its spelling lengths are transcription characters, not measured pen widths. R-031 already established that conditioning draws on whether word lengths fit can reproduce this fact. This related sensitivity uses actual sampled word forms and at most five attempts, rather than unlimited conditional sampling; it adds a finite-retry check, not an independent discovery.
